The softmax function plays a crucial role in the attention mechanism of transformer models. Specifically, it is used to convert the attention scores (which are typically raw dot products between query and key vectors) into a probability distribution over the key vectors. This distribution represents the importance or relevance of each key vector to the corresponding query vector. By normalizing these scores using the softmax function, the model can effectively weigh the contributions of different key-value pairs, allowing it to focus on the most relevant information for making predictions. This mechanism enables the transformer to selectively attend to different parts of the input sequence, making it highly flexible and powerful for various NLP tasks.
